hypotheses.claim: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 (500 ms), the round-2 elite regressed only -0.0014 vs round-1, so the LNS skeleton is near-saturated and objective gains must come from changing WHICH nodes are ruined. Specifically: (a) at low stagnation (iter_frac small, stagnation_ratio~0) the best ruin score is close to a pure removal-savings magnitude rank (cost-efficiency diversification is not yet needed), while (b) at high stagnation the score must shift toward tight-load routes and nodes far from the depot (loose-capacity instances with eccentric depots are the weakest regime at -19.8%/-22.3% VBS gap). A smooth iter_frac/stagnation-driven blend p(iter_frac) from rank-power ~1.0 to ~2.0 combined with gate_load*gate_depot (multiplicative, bounded, product not double-penalized) will beat the round-2 elite's mean objective 16.0804 on the 24 dev instances.

next_search_advice.direction: Exploit stagnation-aware multiplicative gating with load/depot-distance and route-distance gates, but simplify the gate set to reduce double-penalization and emphasize rank-power sharpening only as stagnation grows
